claims.text: High-temperature plastic strain in polycrystalline tungsten is governed by the formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters.
High-temperature toughness in polycrystalline tungsten is governed by the formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters.
Helium irradiation at 500°C forms helium-vacancy clusters in polycrystalline tungsten.
Helium-vacancy clusters are mobile under the stated conditions.
Formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters enhance dislocation glide.
Formation and mobility of helium-vacancy clusters enhance dislocation cross-slip.
Enhanced dislocation glide and cross-slip increase high-temperature plastic strain.
Enhanced dislocation glide and cross-slip increase high-temperature toughness.
Helium-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit significantly greater high-temperature plastic strain than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
Helium-irradiated polycrystalline tungsten will exhibit significantly greater high-temperature toughness than unirradiated polycrystalline tungsten.
The proposed mechanism should hold between 400°C and 600°C.
The proposed mechanism should hold for helium exposures stated as 10^14 to 10^16 ions/cm².
The exact effects of helium-vacancy cluster size and distribution on plastic strain and toughness are not well understood.
